reading.body:
The most useful thing this library offers is five vetted, freely accessible sources for visual explanations of machine learning concepts, covering static diagrams, interactive models, and editable figures for reuse.

The sources split into two practical groups. Distill.pub, The Illustrated Transformer, and Wikimedia Commons are primarily for reading and reference: they explain ideas or supply licensed images. ML Visuals and the Transformer Explainer are for active use: one provides editable figures ready for slides and papers, the other runs a live GPT-2 model in a browser so individual attention heads can be inspected directly.

The transformer architecture receives disproportionate coverage here, appearing in three of the five entries. That reflects where visual explanation has been most needed: the attention mechanism is non-obvious, widely misunderstood, and central to nearly every large language model in production. The data says nothing about hardware photography, benchmark charts, or timelines, which the library name promises but which are not represented in these five items.
